source: Wikipedia event pages + Wikipedia 2026 Iran-war/Lebanon-war/Syria-strikes/Iraq-war/Houthi-strikes timelines + Al Jazeera + Times of Israel + Ynetnews + Amnesty International + ISW + CNBC + CNN + Al Arabiya + France 24 + FDD + Long War Journal + Reuters (syndicated) + Bloomberg + PBS + Cyprus Mail + L'Orient Today + Middle East Monitor + Stars and Stripes + The National + Rudaw + Iraqi News + Kurdistan 24 + Shafaq News, curated 2026-04-21 against events in the 2026-02-28 to 2026-04-21 window
curationNotes: Every entry is sourced from a specific dated article or Wikipedia event page that describes the event at the named location. Reviewer should spot-check the sourceUrl to confirm fit.

Coordinates come from well-documented named facilities (IAEA declarations, OSM, Wikipedia coord tags on airbase/port/refinery/LNG/hotel/consulate/power-station/commando-raid village pages, bridge river crossings) or from Wikipedia's own coordinate tags on the event pages. They are NOT guessed.
Event dates are implied by the source but not stored in this file (the harness is date-agnostic — it only checks that the resolver reproduces the truth lat/lng from the hierarchy).

Entry count widened from the 35-event Iteration-3 set to 50 events after aggressive mining of Yemen/Houthi theater, Syria 2026 Iran-war strike page, Iraq 2026 Iran-war strike page, and Kurdistan Iranian-strikes page — see 27.4-08-CHECKPOINT.md Iteration-4 section for the change log.
Event-type balance: 20 airstrike, 15 on_ground, 8 explosion, 5 targeted, 2 other. All buckets exceed the plan's 10/6/4/3/2 target.

Iteration 4 finding: The canonical pre-2026-war 'Israel-strikes-Iranian-assets-in-Damascus/Aleppo/T-4' pattern was NOT reproduced in the 2026 Iran war window — Syria-theater kinetic events are predominantly Iraqi-militia and Iran-backed-group missile/drone attacks on US bases inside Syria (Qasrok/Al-Tanf/Palmyra T-4), not Israeli strikes on Syrian Iranian assets. The curation honors this and uses the actual Syria-theater pattern rather than padding with the pre-war paradigm. Also: the expected Israeli strikes on Hudaydah port and US strikes on named Sana'a neighborhoods during the war window are sparsely reported in English-language sources; we admitted only the Houthi-on-Israel strikes (which are well-sourced) and did not manufacture Yemen-interior strike entries.

Bellingcat investigations of the 2026 war are not yet indexed for most of these events (war is only ~7 weeks old); mainstream reporting (Al Jazeera, Ynet, Times of Israel, Amnesty, CNBC, Bloomberg, Reuters-syndicated, CNN, Al Arabiya, France 24, PBS, L'Orient Today, Cyprus Mail, Stars and Stripes, Middle East Monitor, Rudaw, Kurdistan 24, Shafaq News, Long War Journal, FDD), dedicated Wikipedia event pages, and the war-timeline pages are the primary verification sources, consistent with the plan's 'Secondary OK' tolerance.

Phase 33 (2026-05-21): additive expectedActor1 / expectedActor2 fields backfilled per ACTOR-04 / D-14 driven by 33-AUDIT-REPORT.md findings. Canonical names sourced verbatim from server/data/actor-catalog.ts ACTOR_CATALOG (e.g. 'Israeli Defense Forces', 'Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps', 'US Armed Forces', 'Hezbollah', 'Houthis', 'Iranian Armed Forces'). Backfill: 50/50 events have non-null expectedActor1 (the war-window source attribution was unambiguous for every entry). events.description: US-Israeli airstrike on Natanz Fuel Enrichment Plant (Shahid Ahmadi Roshan complex); IAEA confirmed damage to entrance buildings of underground enrichment hall. Multiple strikes during the first month of the war.
Israeli airstrike on Fordow underground enrichment facility during late-March escalation wave alongside strikes on Evin Prison and state TV building.
Israeli airstrike on Isfahan nuclear complex uranium conversion facility; IAEA confirmed strike damage. Additional strike reported over Isfahan on April 6, 2026.
Israeli airstrike on Khondab (Arak) heavy water reactor complex; IAEA confirmed facility 'no longer operational' after strike on March 27, 2026.
US airstrike on Kharg Island destroyed more than 90 Iranian military targets — naval mine storage, missile bunkers, air defenses, naval base — while deliberately sparing oil export terminal.

truth.landmark: Kharg Island naval and oil complex

events.description: US cruise-missile airstrike on Shajareh Tayyebeh girls' elementary school and adjacent IRGC compound in Minab, Hormozgan — opening day of war; Amnesty International attributed to a US Tomahawk.
Israeli/US airstrike on Bandar Abbas naval pier (Shahid Bahonar pier area) early in the war; Iranian naval vessel Bandar Lengeh destroyed in port.
Israeli naval strike on an apartment in the Ramada hotel building in central Beirut (Raouche district) killed five senior IRGC Quds Force officers directing Hezbollah and Hamas operations.
US-Israeli airstrikes on Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) positions at Jurf al-Sakhar south of Baghdad on the opening day of the war.
Israeli airstrike on a sports hall in Lamerd, Fars Province during girls' practice on opening day of war (21+ killed).

Iranian ballistic missile with half-ton warhead destroyed Tiferet Israel synagogue and bomb shelter in Ramat Lehi neighbourhood of Beit Shemesh — nine civilians killed; Amnesty called for war-crime probe.
Iranian ballistic missile strikes on Dimona and Arad following US bunker-buster strike on Natanz; ~180 wounded in southern Israel, including 47+ in Dimona near Israel's nuclear research center.
Iranian cluster-munition ballistic missile barrage on Ramat Gan near Tel Aviv killed elderly couple (Yaron and Ilana Moshe) — retaliation for Larijani assassination.

Iranian ballistic missile hit Al Udeid Air Base, Qatar — primary US CENTCOM forward HQ — one of two missiles got through air defenses, no casualties reported. Part of broader barrage of 63 missiles + 11 drones at Qatar.
Cross-border Hezbollah rocket and anti-tank missile attacks on northern Israel; eight IDF soldiers wounded, attacks on Mishmar HaCarmel missile-defense site near Haifa and Upper Galilee sector.
Israeli airstrikes on Hezbollah positions in Dahieh (southern suburbs of Beirut) — 70+ targets struck on March 2 during opening escalation of the 2026 Lebanon war.

Israeli airstrike on Ramlet al-Baida (Beirut) killed Imam Hossein Division commander and Radwan Force southern branch commander — 8 killed, 31 injured; IDF vehicle strike on senior Hezbollah/Quds operative.

Israeli targeted airstrike on outskirts of eastern Tehran killed Ali Larijani (Secretary of Supreme National Security Council), his son Morteza, and office chief Alireza Bayat — most senior Iranian official killed after Khamenei.
Israeli targeted airstrike in Tehran killed Esmail Khatib, Iran's Intelligence Minister — third senior-official assassination in 48 hours (alongside Larijani and Basij commander Soleimani).

Israeli targeted strike on IRGC Navy leadership meeting in Bandar Abbas killed Rear Admiral Alireza Tangsiri (IRGC Navy commander) and Commodore Behnam Rezaei (IRGC Navy intelligence chief) — eliminated top command of Iran's Strait of Hormuz maritime campaign.

Israeli airstrike caused damage to auxiliary building at Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant; Russia's Rosatom evacuated 198 staff; one security personnel killed (fourth strike on the facility in the war per Iranian FM).

Iran launched two intermediate-range ballistic missiles at Diego Garcia US-UK base in Indian Ocean; both failed to strike target (one self-destructed in flight, one intercepted by SM-3) — demonstrated 4,000km+ range previously undisclosed.

Iranian ballistic-missile and drone barrage on opening day of war struck Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) — US Navy Fifth Fleet headquarters in Juffair district of Manama; satellite imagery confirmed extensive destruction of warehouses, radomes, and satellite communications terminals. Part of IRGC 'Operation True Promise 4'.

truth.landmark: Naval Support Activity Bahrain (US Navy Fifth Fleet HQ)

events.description: Iranian drone struck Crowne Plaza hotel in Manama's diplomatic area — five-star hotel complex in central Manama sustained material damage; two US Defense Department employees injured per US State Department; attack came one day after US embassy warning to avoid Manama hotels.

Iranian drone strike on Ras Laffan Industrial City (QatarEnergy LNG complex) — halted world's largest LNG firm's production; European benchmark gas prices surged ~50%, Asian LNG ~39% on the news. Part of two-drone coordinated strike with Mesaieed Industrial City.

truth.landmark: Ras Laffan Industrial City (QatarEnergy LNG complex)

events.description: Iranian drone struck water tank at power plant in Mesaieed Industrial City, Qatar — paired strike with Ras Laffan LNG hit; no casualties reported but prompted QatarEnergy to halt all LNG/associated-product production.

Iranian Shahed-136 drones targeted Saudi Aramco Ras Tanura refinery — Saudi Arabia's largest refinery (>550,000 bpd). Both drones intercepted but debris sparked fire at the complex; facility shut down ~1 week; Brent crude spiked ~7%. Propane/butane exports suspended for weeks.

Iranian-manufactured Shahed-type loitering munition (launched from Lebanon, attributed to Hezbollah) struck hangar at RAF Akrotiri British sovereign base area in Cyprus at ~00:03 local March 2, causing minor damage; prompted partial evacuation. Two additional drones intercepted on March 1 and 4.

truth.admin1: Akrotiri and Dhekelia (UK Sovereign Base Area)

hierarchy.admin1: Akrotiri and Dhekelia (UK Sovereign Base Area)

events.description: Iranian drone struck parking area adjacent to US Consulate General Dubai chancellery at corner of Al Seef Road and Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road (Bur Dubai/Al Seef area), triggering fire near the compound; Secretary Rubio confirmed no injuries. US raised UAE travel advisory.

Israeli helicopter-inserted commando ground raid at Al-Nabi Shayth (Nabi Chit) village in eastern Bekaa Valley; four IDF Sikorsky helicopters crossed Lebanese airspace, two landed; troops searched for remains of navigator Ron Arad (missing since 1986) based on intel from kidnapped Lebanese security official. Accompanying airstrikes on nearby villages killed 41, wounded 40; soldiers failed to locate remains.
events.notes: Phase 27.4.4 Plan 02 correction. Original curator coord (34.0533, 36.2564) was 22km NE of the village center and disagreed with Wikipedia (33°52′20″N 36°06′46″E = 33.87222, 36.11278), Nominatim/OSM, and Asharq Al-Awsat's account of the raid being at the village's eastern cemetery. Updated truth coord to the canonical Wikipedia value. The strike location was within the village; resolver's Nominatim hit at 33.8727,36.1109 lands ~0.1km from the corrected truth.

events.description: Israeli airstrike destroyed Zrarieh Bridge over the Litani River in southern Lebanon — first openly acknowledged Israeli strike on civilian infrastructure in the offensive; IDF justified as cutting Hezbollah north-south movement route.

Israeli airstrike in Jnah neighborhood of Beirut killed Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem — a 'tier-one' Hezbollah commander of the group's southern front, who had inherited the role from Ali Karaki; seven killed, 26 wounded including second- and third-tier commanders and escorts.

Coordinated Israeli strike wave on 100+ sites across Beirut, Bekaa Valley, and southern Lebanon — described as largest concentrated blow against Hezbollah since 2024 pager campaign; 254 killed, 1,165 wounded per Lebanese Civil Defence; strikes targeted Hezbollah command centers per Defence Minister Katz. Occurred hours after US-Iran ceasefire which Netanyahu said did not cover Lebanon.

Israeli airstrike in Nabatieh killed 19 including 13 Lebanese State Security personnel — among deadliest single-strike casualty events for Lebanese state forces during the war; raised Lebanese government fury over targeting of official security institutions.

Iranian missile strike on Mina Salman Port, Bahrain caused fire aboard MT Stena Imperative oil tanker (struck in port) and killed one Bangladeshi worker from falling debris of a separately intercepted missile; AWS data center sustained damage in same wave.

Houthi ballistic-missile strike on Beersheba area triggered air-defense sirens and was intercepted by Israeli air defenses — the attack marked the Houthis' entry into the 2026 Iran war after four weeks on the sidelines; sirens also went off around Israel's main nuclear research center in Dimona.

Houthi cruise missile and UAV barrage targeting Eilat intercepted by IDF on March 28, 2026 — hours after the Beersheba ballistic-missile launch; the Houthis claimed they targeted 'vital and military' sites in the Red Sea resort city as part of their formal entry into the Iran war.

Houthi cluster-warhead ballistic missile aimed at Ben Gurion Airport fell in open area in southern Israel on April 4, 2026 — no casualties; Houthis claimed the strike was coordinated with Iran's IRGC and Hezbollah targeting 'Ben Gurion Airport and vital military sites in southern Israel'.

Houthi cruise-missile and UAV barrage on Eilat on April 6, 2026 — several UAVs intercepted by IDF with contact lost on others; Houthis framed as coordinated operation with Iran and Hezbollah against 'vital and military sites' in Eilat.

Unidentified airstrikes (US/Israeli, attributed by PMF to American aircraft) on Popular Mobilization Forces 19th Brigade (Harakat Ansar Allah al-Awfiya) bases in the Akashat area of Al-Qa'im District, western Anbar — hit brigade medical unit, second-regiment headquarters, and logistical support facility. At least 35 fighters killed and ~90 wounded in one of the deadliest single-day strikes of the war in Iraq.
events.notes: Phase 27.4.4 Plan 02: known sparse-OSM ceiling event (~100km miss in resolver-only mode). Truth coord 33.33,41.0 corresponds to the Akashat phosphate-mine + PMF-19 base area in Al-Qa'im District (Wikipedia: 33°20'N 41°00'E). Nominatim has no entry for the mine, the PMF base, or any place at that coord — reverse-geocoding 33.33,41.0 returns 'Al-Rutba Central Subdistrict'. The query 'Akashat, Al Anbar, Iraq' returns a different settlement (also called Akashat) at 33.67,39.97 in Al-Rutba District, ~100km west-northwest of the strike location. The LocationHierarchyV2 schema has no admin2/district field to disambiguate. In production, ctx.bellingcatCoord (from extractBellingcatGeo on article text) would override this if the source contains explicit coords; the resolver-only eval cannot reach that path. Treat this event's miss as the honest sparse-OSM ceiling for the corpus, not a resolver bug.

events.description: US airstrike on Popular Mobilization Forces command headquarters at Habbaniyah in Al Anbar Governorate killed 15 PMF fighters including Anbar Operations commander Saad Dawai al-Baiji, wounded 30+ — described as deadliest attack in Iraq since the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran on February 28. A follow-up A-10 strike on March 25 killed seven more Iraqi soldiers.

Iran-backed militia drone strike on Umm Qasr Naval Base in Basra Governorate — four drones targeted the naval facility's radar system, igniting fire, minor damage, no casualties reported; one of the first strikes on Iraqi naval infrastructure in the war.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched five ballistic missiles at Al-Harir Air Base (a.k.a. Harir Military Base) near Erbil in Iraqi Kurdistan, hosting US forces; struck in early-morning twin-wave pattern (~04:00 and ~08:30). Impact on US bases assessed as limited with no reported casualties, but extensive air-defense activity over Erbil International Airport.

Six Iranian ballistic missiles struck Area Command One of the Peshmerga forces in the Soran administration of Erbil province — killed six Peshmerga soldiers and wounded 30+; President Nechirvan Barzani stated Iran privately admitted the strike was carried out 'by mistake' and condemned it as 'direct hostile aggression against the sovereignty of the country'.

Drone strike on the residence of Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani in Duhok caused damage but no casualties (Barzani was not present). The US State Department condemned the attack as a 'despicable terrorist attack by Iran's terrorist militia proxies in Iraq'; Iraqi PM al-Sudani opened a federal investigation.

US-attributed targeted strike in Baghdad killed Abu Ali al-Askari — Kataib Hezbollah's long-serving security chief and spokesperson who publicly planned attacks on US interests. Kataib Hezbollah confirmed his death but did not publicly specify circumstances; Iraqi reporting attributed the strike to US forces during the 2026 Iran war.

Iraqi-origin missile barrage from Kataib Jund al-Karrar scored a direct hit on Tiyas (T-4) Air Base near Palmyra, Syria — the US-coalition-presence base struck from across the border. Same day the militia claimed a drone attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan; Iraqi-Iranian militias emerged as the primary actor striking US positions inside Syria.

Iraqi-militia drone strike (six drones, launched from Tell al-Hawa by Islamic Resistance in Iraq) on Kharab al-Jir military base in Hasakah Governorate — targeted US-coalition-presence site; Syrian-Iraqi intelligence coordination opened to arrest perpetrators. Part of the cross-border Iraqi-militia-on-US-bases-in-Syria pattern that defined the Syria theater of the war.

Iranian ballistic missile direct hit on seven-story residential building in Haifa, Israel — four civilians killed (Vladimir and Lena Gershovitz, son Dima, daughter-in-law Lucille Jane) when their building collapsed; IDF probed the air-defense failure that let the missile through.

Iranian ballistic missile barrage struck the Bazan Group (Oil Refineries Ltd.) refinery in Haifa Bay — direct hit on a gasoline storage tank roof; fire contained with no casualties, no hazardous materials release. Second strike on the facility since the war began; Israeli Energy Ministry subsequently pushed to relocate rather than close the refinery.

truth.landmark: Bazan Group oil refinery (Oil Refineries Ltd.)
